problem_type: Automated repair PRs lack executable required checks and a stable review identity
symptom: Repeated bot docs PRs #604/#631/#632/#634/#635/#637/#638 remain BLOCKED without Quality Gate runs.
direct_cause: The workflow carries the old direct-push skip marker into PR commits, uses GITHUB_TOKEN without explicit CI dispatch, and names branches by main SHA.
class_root: The automated publication boundary does not own both stable PR identity and required-check scheduling.
affected_population: Every main push requiring index/status/ledger repair
Manual repair reruns and updates to already-open repair PRs

external_sources.purpose: Default token recursion protection and explicit dispatch exception
Action uses force-with-lease, incompatible with this task restriction

invariants: One fixed docs/autosync head has at most one open PR.
Every published repair schedules the existing full Quality Gate using workflow_dispatch.
No CI skip markers, direct main writes, forced pushes, or duplicated validation workflow.
The regenerated current-main tree is authoritative; previous generated heads remain ancestors of ordinary pushes.
generality_proof: Both automatic and manual entries converge on the same publish step. Tests execute that shell against a local bare Git remote for initial creation, repeated equal output, main advancement, no-diff closure, and failed dispatch recovery.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own fixed-branch publication and explicit CI scheduling after the three repair gates.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Every main push uses the common serialized autosync job.
Manual retry uses exactly the same publication and dispatch step.

recurrence.reason: Each successive main SHA produced another blocked PR; seven observed instances.
same_class_scan: rg autosync and skip ci across .github/workflows, scripts and docs/lessons; inspected initial creation and PR migration commits.
Inspected SEO Radar (fixed branch without skip marker but same token caveat) and download-stats (non-PR data branch); this change is scoped to docs repair publication.

prevention.invariant: Every repair goes through fixed PR publication followed by explicit official CI dispatch.
prevention.failure_mode: Repair gate, normal push, gh API or dispatch failure exits the job nonzero.
prevention.strategy: Use token recursion protection and explicit dispatch rather than disabling checks; retain branch ancestry for ordinary pushes.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove SHA-suffixed PR producer, CI skip markers, and force-pushing create-pull-request action from docs autosync.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Remove create-pull-request from this workflow because its current implementation force-pushes. No replacement dependency; Git and gh shipped on the hosted runner execute documented native operations.

migration: Close superseded legacy automatic PRs with comments, retain and explicitly dispatch CI on newest #638. After this fix merges, subsequent new repairs use docs/autosync. No rewriting legacy heads or merging PRs.
residual_risks: Full workflow_dispatch retains the existing expensive all-surfaces policy; failures on unrelated surfaces remain real failures.
Until this PR merges, main still has the old producer and can create additional legacy PRs.
SEO Radar is outside this docs-autosync repair; its default-token PR trigger still has the official approval caveat.
Git fixtures prove publication behavior; GitHub execution and final checks are reported separately.
